Thomas Frank has teased that there is more to the story of his torrid time at Tottenham he will be willing to tell once he has steered Crystal Palace back on course.

The 53-year-old was prepared for plenty of questions about his past employers when he was unveiled to the media on Thursday afternoon ahead of Saturday’s trip to Coventry, acknowledging “I know today is a lot about me”.

The Danish boss helped stabilise Brentford in the Premier League, and was nominated for the league’s Manager of the Year award while with the Bees, but could not replicate the same success at Spurs and was sacked after just under eight months in charge.

“It’s something I’ve… maybe one day I’ll tell a little bit more about it,” mentioned Frank, whose deal through June 2029 was confirmed on Monday.

Industry observers note that “I understand why it’s also interesting. I think it’s more about Palace in general today. What can I say? I always said the day I got sacked, I’ll have time to travel, so I think I was relatively quick over it.

“But of course you want success, and I’m competitive, so I think that answer probably demands a little bit more time, which I am happy to do one day.”.

For now, Frank – who spent his time off in Japan, Australia and Denmark – has to figure out what to do with a side resuming their Premier League season in last place, while also balancing a Europa League campaign that continues next Thursday at home against Real Sociedad.

On Thursday, Palace confirmed two additions to the new boss’ backroom staff, with Justin Cochrane joining as first-team coach and Chris Haslam as fitness and athletic performance coach.

Cochrane worked with Frank at both Brentford and Tottenham, and is at the moment part of Thomas Tuchel’s England set-up, while Haslam was previously the head of athletic performance at Frank’s former employers Brentford, and also works as a fitness coach with the Danish FA.

Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva was also confirmed as part of Frank’s team on Friday morning, with existing staff Paddy McCarthy, the assistant manager, and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy retained.

Frank is a firm believer that “culture is everything”, and boils down his philosophy to a “no dickheads” approach to crafting a cohesive, successful environment.

Asked about claims that his success at Brentford had more to do with the model, he replied: “Let’s put it this way: I think I was pretty notable in terms of building that model.”.

He has no qualms about what he has witnessed so far from a squad he is still getting to know as many have recently returned from international duty.

Frank added: “The players were buzzing. That told me, ‘Oh, that’s good. They like to be together’. That’s very key, because it’s been tough times until now.

“Hopefully we can just continue, but there will also be ups and downs in games and whatever, and that’s why we need each other.”.

If there was any doubt over the scale of the task facing Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford, a social media exchange between one of his players and a content creator has illustrated it perfectly.

Manchester United winger Amad Diallo responded directly to an Instagram account criticising his recent display.

Recent findings suggest that “Just shut your mouth, bro - you’re talking too much now,” Diallo wrote. “Go play in my place if it bothers you that much”.

While it is understandable for a young player to feel the weight of fan frustration, the optics of the situation are poor.

A Manchester United player reacting publicly to a troll on social media just days before a new manager takes charge is an indictment of the dressing room’s current mental state.

Recent findings suggest that 🚨📲 𝗡𝗘𝗪: Amad Diallo’s comment on a fan who criticized him: “Just shut your mouth, bro—you’re talking too much now. Go play in my place if it bothers you that much.” https://t.co/sLqd3B912HNovember 18, 2026.

The incoming Pochettino will want an emotionally resilient squad, given the responsibility of representing one of the biggest clubs in world football.

This incident highlights the repair job required at Carrington, because if a highly-rated 24-year-old is spending his free time scrolling through his own mentions and biting back at criticism, it begs a much larger, more worrying question: Are all Manchester United players this hyper-aware of their online reception?

If they are, it explains a great deal about the fragility on display during matches. A squad that lives and dies by its social media mentions is unequipped to handle the pressure cooker environment that is Old Trafford.

When things go wrong on the pitch - and they frequently do for this current iteration of Man United - players affected by outside noise are far more likely to retreat into their shells than rally together.

Sources indicate that pochettino’s first priority therefore cannot be tactical; it must be cultural. He has to insulate his squad from the news cycle which bounces between online praise and vitriol. The Argentine could do a lot worse than instituting a bunker mentality from day one at Old Trafford.

Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized blueprint is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it.
  • Recent findings suggest that rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise.
  • LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized blueprint is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Recent findings suggest that rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Industry observers note that rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

"I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she said Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

According to recent reports, five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

It has been revealed that "I'm so excited," she noted. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

According to recent reports, rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan said. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

In a recent development, "We have these big red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

In a recent development, "I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman said. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many latest players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

It has been revealed that "Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone said. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a upcoming construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly notable for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

"She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Newly introduced York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

Industry observers note that "She's fun, she's engaging," Stone noted. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

Rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

Industry observers note that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The international break is over, and it's now time to get back to the usual business with European soccer resuming alongside the MLS playoffs in the United States. It was supposed to be a quiet break, but that wasn't the case at all, since Manchester United decided to part ways with Michael Carrick and appointed Mauricio Pochettino, who had recently signed a new deal with the United States men's national team but decided to leave after the break. Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid will battle with Barcelona for the LaLiga title, while Como are still one of the most interesting sides to watch in the near future. Let's now take a look at the five teams to watch after the break, starting with the Red Devils.

The biggest change of the break: Manchester United sacked coach and club legend Michael Carrick and replaced him with Pochettino, who makes his Premier League comeback after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. As the English giants are currently sitting 18th in the standings, this is a major task for the now-former USMNT head coach, who will make his return at Anfield against Liverpool in his opening game at United. It's a daunting start in one of the most hostile atmospheres in the country. Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are arguably entering their prime and appear ready to take the team to the next level, supported by a number of exciting young prospects who could play a key role in shaping the club's future. Will Mourinho be able to win a trophy in his first season back at the club? That would be a story.

Recent findings suggest that if there is one team to watch in Serie A, it's Como. The side led by Cesc Fabregas is impressing both domestically and in Europe, as it is presently fourth in the league-phase standings of the UEFA Champions League. Fabregas can count on some of the best players in the league, such as Nico Paz, the Argentine talent who is now also expected to lead the national team after Lionel Messi's retirement. The question is how far Como can go this season, given that playing every three days can be a big challenge for players who have never experienced it. It has been revealed that it's always about Manchester City: the Citizens are still waiting to learn what sanctions they will face after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. They are facing a challenging season that might have an impact on the years ahead. It's not clear what the sanctions will be, but we will likely know more before the end of the current season. On the pitch, they are also facing a season of changes as longtime coach Pep Guardiola left the club in the summer and was replaced by Enzo Maresca, who is now overseeing that transition.

Recent findings suggest that spanish soccer is not just about Real Madrid and Barcelona: Atletico Madrid are once again near the top of the standings, five points behind the Blaugrana. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's admission to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe was working as a spy for China could have profound implications for the $5 trillion (€4.47 trillion) tech giant.

The Financial Times first reported on Huang's affair with Alice H., an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia, which has been suspected of trying to circumvent export controls to get advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The newspaper reported that the US government and its intelligence community believe she was recruited as a spy by China's Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US government officials drafted a memo about the allegations shortly before US President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping in May.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy has exposed him and the organization to criticism that it may have allowed China to obtain valuable trade secrets as Beijing tries to gain an edge in the race to develop advanced AI models.

Sources indicate that nvidia is initiating an investigation led by independent board members and an external law firm. It stated in a statement that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.".

It has been revealed that "The board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," the organization said Sunday. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information.".

The organization's shares fell in early trading on Monday.

While US intelligence officials have not commented publicly on the claims, Trump — with whom Jensen Huang has a close relationship — has backed the Nvidia boss.

It has been revealed that "He's an honorable guy," said Trump. "I have not spoken to him ​about it. I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine.".

Tim Culpan, an Asia tech reporter who has covered Nvidia and Huang closely for years, told DW that while Nvidia's fundamental strengths as a organization remain in place, Huang is hugely personally damaged by the story.

"They're still going to make great chips and they're going to sell them to millions of customers around the world who want the best AI chips in the world," he mentioned.

Industry observers note that "His opinion is going to carry a lot less weight now. And that, in the long term, will flow through to Nvidia and Nvidia's own corporate interests. So it won't be immediate. It's really a fact that he doesn't have the sway or the power that he might have had one week ago simply through this.".

Richard Windsor, a tech analyst and the founder of research firm Radio Free Mobile, said the news could be very serious for Nvidia given how much the company has revolved around Huang for decades.

"This problem is particularly acute because Jensen Huang is very hands-on, meaning that the key decisions that led to its success were ultimately taken by him and because there is no obvious successor," he stated.

"I suspect we are about to find out just how much the market thinks that the tech giant is dependent on its iconic founder and CEO.".

Nvidia and Huang's attitude toward China and potential Chinese customers has been a bone of contention with US intelligence officials — despite Huang's close relationship with Trump.

According to recent reports, huang has repeatedly lobbied Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. A 2025 export control deal heavily curbed sales, but Trump subsequently permitted the export of older H200 Nvidia chips to China in return for the US government receiving a cut of the sales.

However, that deal has been complicated and bogged down by Washington's strict export-license review. China has also initiated import controls, despite strong demand from Chinese companies. China lacks access to the most advanced AI-capable chips. Beijing wants to develop its own alternatives but has struggled to catch up.

Huang has argued that Chinese dependence on Nvidia's chips would prevent rivals such as Huawei from catching up and boosting China's ambitions to dominate AI supply chains.

Industry observers note that however, that argument has been dismissed by many US intelligence officials. They fear that unlimited Chinese access to the most advanced Nvidia chips would boost China's domestic AI sector, lead to its AI models catching up with the leading US models and see the chips being used in Chinese military applications.

Sources indicate that the US-China rivalry has become a central theme in the global AI story, with both countries seeking to gain an upper hand in the technology. Leading US AI executives such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei have argued that US AI companies can't afford to take a prolonged pause to allow safety standards in AI to catch up, if they're going to prevent Chinese firms from gaining an advantage.

Washington's central fear over Huang's affair is that it could have led to Beijing obtaining vital trade secrets or other key information about how Nvidia makes its most advanced chips.

In a recent development, windsor thinks Huang will survive the "severe test" due to his importance to the manufacturer. He also cast doubt on the extent to which Beijing and its leading tech firms have learned from Nvidia's chips, pointing to China's own chip ambitions and commitment to have its firms buy its own semiconductors.

"I am far from convinced that Chinese AI has materially benefited from technology or illicit chip imports that it gained from Nvidia," he said.

The news comes at a particularly challenging moment for Nvidia, which has benefited massively from the AI boom thanks to its position as the leading maker of cutting-edge semiconductors needed for AI applications.

Nvidia's valuation has soared dramatically in recent years as companies rushed to buy its chips, becoming the world's first $5 trillion company in October 2025.

It has been revealed that however, doubts over the sustainability of the $9 trillion capital expenditure AI boom have sparked a major sell-off in stocks related to the boom in recent weeks. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the US midterms have added to the doubts, given the strength of voter opposition to data center construction in the US.

A drone operator ​who filmed Manchester United's training session this week has apologised for what he called a "total error of judgment" and removed the footage from ⁠his YouTube channel.

The footage, filmed at United's Carrington training ground during newly introduced manager Mauricio Pochettino's first training session on Thursday, was uploaded online under the username "CC OVERVIEW".

In a statement ⁠posted on his YouTube channel ​on ⁠Friday, the drone operator stated that while the flight was legal under drone regulations, filming ⁠the session had been "unethical".

“My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time,” he wrote.

“I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.”.

According to recent reports, the operator added that he had wrongly assumed that the training session would be open to various media outlets. Pochettino’s first session was closed to the press.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match,” he stated.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel.

“I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos.”.

In a recent development, the footage has nevertheless been shared across social media and garnered millions of views. United have not commented on the matter.

United have a strict no drones policy and have signs around Carrington warning that anyone caught using a drone "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".

Pochettino arrived from ‌the US men's national team ⁠this week after United sacked Michael Carrick, ⁠and faces an immediate test with a trip to Liverpool on ‌Sunday.

United are languishing 18th in the league table after winning just one of their 10 games, while Liverpool sit fourth.

In recent years, Louisville City FC have been one of the most successful regular-season teams in United Soccer League history, but it hasn't translated to winning the major game. They haven't won the USL Championship since 2018, and while this season has been a trying time dealing with injuries and a upcoming coach taking over, they're playing their best soccer when it matters to set up a strange clash with Sacramento Republic at noon Eastern on Saturday. What's strange isn't that it's Louisville and Sacramento meeting, but that the match kicks off at 9 a.m. local time, a time Louisville forward Ray Serrano notes he hasn't played soccer at since he was 15. While it's a regular training time for Louisville and they'll try to keep things on an East Coast timeline, it's hard not to take the shift into account when planning for a final.

Industry observers note that it's a challenge that comes with the desire to reach as many fans as possible with a final of this magnitude. Leagues have to work with broadcast networks to ensure that the slots work, and for the USL, having the game on CBS is worth the risk of a 9 a.m. local start with a West Coast team hosting. It's nothing Louisville won't be prepared for, as they look to keep their internal clocks on Eastern Standard Time.

In a recent development, "No, we're trying to stay on Eastern Time, so for us, it's training time," defender Kyle Adams remarked. "Wake up at 8:00 a.m., but really it's 5:00 a.m. Go to sleep a little bit earlier. Try to do everything really just to stay on Eastern Time, eat a little bit earlier on the night before, and just treat it as going into training, and then get after them.".

Recent findings suggest that other teams have dealt with similar challenges, like the Los Angeles Rams when playing an NFL game in Australia, but it's still a struggle to deal with en route to a cup final as Louisville look to reach the pinnacle of the sport for the first time since 2018. Winners of the Prinx Tires USL Cup during the regular season, they do have cup experience that will prove to be fruitful in this competition, which Adams noted has been something that brings the injury-riddled squad together. "We know in the last few years we've struggled in these knockout games, but this year we've turned it on," Serrano remarked. "It has been really good preparation, just the mentality of going into them, how we deal with the pressure, and we're seeing the fruits of all that now.".

It's cliche to say that because of the adversity that they've dealt with, the club is playing its best soccer when it matters, but between using four goalkeepers during the season and seeing manager Danny Cruz depart to be an assistant manager with Minnesota United, it hasn't been an easy task for interim manager Simon Bird to get this team on the right track at this critical juncture.

Industry observers note that "Going back to the main part is the adversity that we've faced. You mentioned injuries, having to deal with that side of it, some of the various parts of the season, different things we've had to deal with from a tactical or technical standpoint, where we've lost games, and we feel that we shouldn't have lost games," Bird said when reflecting on the team's development under his leadership. "The most impressive thing I said to the guys today, yesterday in training, we worked on our defensive structure, but the whole training session I thought was excellent, not just the defensive side, off the ball but with the ball, and to see it all come together towards the end of the season is really rewarding. Hopefully, we can carry that on and put together a complete performance, and that's what we've had throughout the season-moments where we've let ourselves down in all these different areas, set pieces, maybe transition at other times, in front of goal. So, putting it all together for a complete performance on Saturday is the goal.".

Traveling away to a tough environment in Heart Health Park, Louisville will meet the hottest team in the league in Sacramento Republic. They've ridden a club-record 16-game unbeaten run to the final based on their defense. That has set a strong foundation to build on, and it could make the final one where the first team to score a goal wins the match. Sacramento's squad also has experience in USL Cup finals, which goes a long way when preparing for games of this stature.

In a recent development, "I don't think it can hurt to have that. This would be a step forward for my first final. I think experience is invaluable for players and for staff," Sacramento coach Neil Collins remarked. "But then there's also the recognition that every game is different, every team is different, and every season is different. So it's just trying to get the balance right and enjoy the opportunity. You've got to have the mechanisms to control the things you can control. Obviously, the opposition team is trying to do the same, and we've got to do everything we can to be ready to take the opportunity when it comes. But the experience will definitely help us; there's plenty of that in our dressing room.".

It's a final where the best that the league has to offer will be on display, and it couldn't come at a better time. The summer of soccer, with the United States hosting the World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada, has truly turned into a soccer avalanche, and this final showcases one of the top atmospheres in the league. You can't ask for much better than that, as no matter what, a drought will come to an end. Sacramento Republic haven't won the final since 2014, while Louisville haven't won since 2018, and for these clubs, it will mean a lot to get back to the top.

#25215. 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border.
  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

"November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

Recent findings suggest that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how swiftly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a new one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

Recent findings suggest that the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

Among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

Industry observers note that today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

Industry observers note that at the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very quickly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

Meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

In his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he said, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an issue that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

His photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

Sources indicate that menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he said.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

Sources indicate that according to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she mentioned. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

According to recent reports, the story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist noted she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

It has been revealed that in particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she said. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

It has been revealed that could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, remarked Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

Industry observers note that "In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," noted Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical complications, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

"It's very vital to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," said Feuchtenberger.

Industry observers note that "For me personally, the whole glitch of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

According to recent reports, moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she said. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

It has been revealed that "This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," noted Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth.
  • This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Industry observers note that astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth.

This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond.

Industry observers note that astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA.

Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year. Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space.

In a recent development, for perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement.

By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft.

The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical complications and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe.

Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977. Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day.

According to recent reports, even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2, which rolled out in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035.

As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space, their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges that come with sending spacecraft ever farther into the cosmos.

Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy.
  • Recent findings suggest that the big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area.
  • Recent findings suggest that “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy. Mikel Arteta’s instant simmering fury at being denied a first-half penalty may also have turned into something rather more explosive had Martin Odegaard not later sent the champions six points clear with a ninth win in 10 Premier League games.

Recent findings suggest that the big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area. Which came first? The intervention of VAR suggested the latter. But Hallam duly went to check the pitch-side monitor before then announcing the former.

Recent findings suggest that “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared. Cue cheers from the home Arsenal crowd. “However…,” he went on. “Red No 29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City.”.

Recent findings suggest that #ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

Sources indicate that it all sounded so decisive that most inside the Emirates instinctively thought the outcome reasonable. But then came a closer look at the rules. And Law 11.2 certainly did seem to support Arteta’s protestations: “In situations where a player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

It has been revealed that arteta clearly saw no value after the match in aiming much criticism at Hallam following a fourth 1-0 win in 10 league games, but did still emphasise his surprise at the decision. “What do you think?” he asked one reporter. “I thought offside, but the law says that doesn’t matter,” replied the journalist. “So not offside then,” stated Arteta, who stressed that he needs to understand “what is overruling what in the decision-making” after a Premier League statement simply said that Havertz was deemed offside “in the build-up”.

It has been revealed that at the very best, it all leaves further confusion and again opens refereeing body Pro Ref to the charge of inconsistency. Fabian Schär, for example, was awarded a penalty for Newcastle against Bournemouth in 2024, despite being in an offside position when his shirt was grabbed by Adam Smith.

Conversely, Dango Ouattara had a penalty overturned for Brentford against Leeds last season after going down under pressure from Gabriel Gudmundsson before being deemed offside. The crucial point seems to be whether the player has actually challenged for the ball at the time of the infringement and, in this case, the answer was surely “no”.

Premier League title triumphs, however, are often forged on forgettable wins in frustrating circumstances and this was ultimately a classic of the genre. With Noni Madueke continuing to step up superbly in the absence of Bukayo Saka, Arsenal’s combination of attacking persistence and defensive resilience was ultimately rewarded by Odegaard’s scrappy 72nd-minute shot. For young players, it was also every bit as educational as the VAR controversy might be for emerging officials.

Madueke’s low shot forced a save by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, but Odegaard was somehow first to the rebound, despite being the wrong side of the penalty spot and five yards behind Hull defender John Egan when the ball was struck.

“The way he scores, not the most beautiful, but the most effective,” noted Arteta, who said that his team had sometimes tried too hard for a “perfect goal” and should instead be happy with something “more pragmatic”.

Sources indicate that it was a well-judged assessment as Arsenal head into the international break with creative deficiencies, but still almost flawless in the cold hard currency of results. Three wins in three days, including at Anfield and in Prague, also underlines a certain champions mentality.

It has been revealed that “I need to praise the players,” said Arteta. “It’s been very very demanding; very short time to recover with all the travel. The mentality is incredible. It’s still going to be super difficult. We can improve in a number of areas.”.

When it was then put to him that Arsenal have been offside 35 times this season – with Havertz responsible for 15 of those – Arteta acknowledged that “timing” was one element. But, with Havertz targeted by some frustrated fans, he stressed that responsibility was always shared for those split-second moments by the passer and receiver.

It has been revealed that he also singled out Madueke, again easily Arsenal’s most creative player, following his surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. “He went away, started to train, he came back and it was a different Noni,” said Arteta, of his reaction to also being out of the Arsenal team earlier in the season. “You could sense that he meant business and he wasn’t going to accept the situation and, since then, I think he’s been incredible.”.

An improved showing by Jaissle’s Newcastle, but they will be dissapointed that they failed to see it through after Jacob Murphy scored in the 80th minute.

Arsenal far from their best, but it is another one-goal win in the Premier League. They are now six points clear at the top of the Premier League, and it is 27 points from the first 30 available.

It has been revealed that another save at Craven Cottage, this time from Hornicek to keep out a sweet strike from Sessegnon at the edge of the box. Moments earlier, Dedic brought down Muniz at the edge of the box.

Sources indicate that one last change by Arteta: Zubmimendi on for Guimaraes. Madueke could have made the points safe after slick interplay involving Eze and Merino around the edge of the box. Tried to be clever with the finish, the goalkeeper’s save was deflected back towards the goal and it was hacked off the line.

Leno gets down swiftly to deny Lewis Hall as Newcastle pour forward in search of the winner.

As good as Murphy’s goal was, Rodrigo Muniz’s finish with the outside of his foot may well be better. Newcastle’s lead was short-lived.

And they have immediately conceded an equaliser, Rodrigo Munoz with a smart close range finish but Newcastle were be mortified with the defending.

Not for the first time Will Osula’s weak hold up play gives the ball back to Fulham but Newcastle had plenty of men back and failed to clear.

According to recent reports, jacob Murphy has scored the goal that some of Newcastle’s earlier good play deserved. Cut inside on to his weaker left foot, and curled a shot beyond Leno from 20 yards.

Newcastle finally have their goal and what a strike it is from Jacob Murphy. A loose pass from Cesar Palacios in midfield gifted possession to the Newcastle winger and he ran forward, cut inside on to his left foot and curled a shot beyond the reach of Leno from 25 yards.

Arsenal’s captain dinks over Tzolakis after Hull’s goalkeeper saved Madueke’s shot. Odeegard was on the move while the defenders were on their heels. Relief at the Emirates, this has been hard work for the champions. Can Hull muster a response?

In a recent development, this is about as dominant as Newcastle have been in a game all season but they have not been able to find a goal from some where. They have just gone close again as Will Osula just fails to reach Amar Dedic’s cross.

Recent findings suggest that arteta has made another double sub: Hincapie and Eze replace Tzolis and Calafiori, so all change down the left flank. For Hull, Lucas Herrington has replaced the injured Semi Ajayi at the back.

Industry observers note that felt like the cheers for Viktor Gyokeres to replace Kai Havertz were as much a reflection on frustrations with the German as enthusiasm for the Swede. Havertz has struggled today and is far less convincing in this sort of match – when the onus is more on the Arsenal to create – than he was in scoring the winner at Anfield last Sunday.

Specific explanation for Declan Rice’s substitution is unclear – he didn’t look injured – and so perhaps just reflection of risks associated with a third 90 minutes in six days alongside an acknowledgement of quality alternatives on the bench.

Some changes at the Emirates: Cho and Lewie Coyle are replaced by Joe Gelhardt and Brooke Norton-Cuffy.

Arteta with a double sub: Gyokeres and Merino on for Havertz and Rice, which comes as something of a surprise.

It has been revealed that hull’s goalkeeper Tzolakis has just saved with his feet to deny Madueke. A few minutes earlier, Konsa blocked a Cho shot after a threatening Hull break. Still no opening goal.

It has been all Newcastle at the start of the second half and Harvey Barnes has now failed to take a hat-trick of chances. This was the best of the lot, running on to the ball, middle of the area from a perfectly weighted Yoane Wissa pass, he blasted a shot the wrong side of the post.

In a recent development, the second halves at the Emirates and Craven Cottage have kicked off. No changes from Arsenal, Hull, Fulham or Newcastle.

While Kai Havertz was in an offside position when his shirt was pulled, he may not have been active.

The law states: “A player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

However, the Premier League match centre does not see it that way.

#ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

Sources indicate that frustrating first half for Arsenal, but it was never going to be easy to go again in the Premier League following a Champions League away game and last Sunday’s massive win against Liverpool. Hull have also played with confidence and resolve.

Hopefully there will be more action in the second 45 minutes at Craven Cottage and the Emirates.

An odd moment at the Emirates. Referee Farai Hallam was sent to monitor to look at a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the Hull box. Through his headset, he tells the crowd that a “holding offence” has been committed – cue cheers from the Arsenal fans – before adding “however, the Arsenal player was in an offside position”. So no penalty. It would have been very soft in any case, Havertz was not close to reaching the rebound from a long shot.

Mikel Arteta predictably furious to not get a penalty, even though Havertz was clearly offside before being pulled.

According to recent reports, I’ve spotted something else since I was covering Arsenal in 2018. I was gazing up at the boards that circle the top tier where the club mark every trophy that the team has won. There was previously this massive gap, of course, from 2005 until 2014 before the cabinet gradually began refilling. But someone has since had a good idea. They have added all the women’s trophies as well, transforming the tally by just the odd 17 during those tricky years of transition and billionaire rivals owners in the men’s game.

Declan Rice has also just had a shot flash wide, but still no clear chances for either team.

Dan Burn thought he had scored from close-range, but Wissa has been penalised for blocking Castagne so the goal was ruled out.

#FULNEW – 33' The referee's call of no goal to Newcastle United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Wissa fouled Castagne in the build-up. AR2: "Defensive foul at the back post. Wissa holding at the back post". REF: "Castagne held back by Wissa. It's a deliberate foul". VAR: "He's clearly holding him - confirming the on-field decision of defensive free-kick. Wissa is clearly making an attempt to hold the Fulham defender. Clear holding offence".

It has been revealed that some controversy here as Newcastle appear to have had a perfectly good goal ruled out for an innocuous looking foul from Yoane Wissa on Timothy Costagne inside the box. Dan Burn was the scorer. Newcastle’s bench are furious. Most of us are just bemused.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal have largely been on top after Hull’s lively start but clear chances are scarce and Hull’s fans certainly sound increasingly confident. “You’re only here for the Tigers”, they say. To which a rendition of “champions” rings out. On that note, they had a replica of the Premier League trophy outside the Emirates before the match, with fans queuing up to get their photo with it.

The bright start from the visitors has not been maintained and Fulham have been on top for the last few minutes. Lukasz Hornicek just made a full-stretch save to deny Oscar Bobb and there is a sense inside the stadium that the first goal is coming.

Newcastle, as we have seen all too often recently, really struggle to pass through the lines and when the ball makes it out wide it invariably seems to go backwards again.

It has been revealed that although Harvey Barnes has just forced a good save from Leno from a Jacob Murphy cross. It was easily Newcastle’s best move of the match as Wissa and Osula linked up for the first time through the middle.

According to recent reports, david Raya to Arsenal’s rescue, plucking Stroud’s shot away from the bottom corner after a Calafiori giveaway. This has been a positive opening 20 minutes from Hull.

Arsenal with a penalty shout, turned down.

Sources indicate that kai Havertz was going away from goal but Nobel Medy hardly subtle with his challenge – arm and leg – on the edge of the area. It would have been what we call soft but the sort of innocuous challenge that very often results in a foul elsewhere on the pitch.

On a self-indulgent note, this is an all-too-rare trip to the Emirates for me. I covered Arsenal for the last decade of the Arsene Wenger era, ending in 2018 and haven’t made many visits since. A few things are already striking: so many familiar faces still among the staff at a club that has always had more of a family feel than most. Outside, and few of the gaps in the middle (or top tier) that became evident during the final Wenger years when many fans clearly lost faith in the team’s title-winning credentials. The atmosphere is a notch up too.

Sources indicate that thiaw heads wide after a well-worked short corner from Newcastle, but the flag is up for offside in any case. Lewis Hall with the cross.

A decent start from Newcastle United against Fulham and you can see clearer patterns of play emerging. The fact that Fulham are constantly looking to build their attacks by playing out from the back has also helped. The home side have had a couple of scares already.

Hull gain some territory in the early exchanges, and win a corner via a long throw. From the set-piece, Egan’s set-piece hit the side-netting. A shot across Arsenal’s bows.

According to recent reports, the lack of Mohamed Beloloumi’s creative spark clearly a big blow for Hull against the best defence in the league; a defence that will be further strengthened by the imminent return of William Saliba. Mikel Arteta had decided that Saliba would be better served by playing against Aston Villa for the Under-21s at Boreham Wood tomorrow. Hull have started on the front, though, in the opening minutes.

Recent findings suggest that updates to follow from the Emirates and Craven Cottage. The Last Post was played and there was a minute’s silence as both grounds mark Remembrance Day.

It’s always great to be back home. It’s the last game before the international break so we know the importance of that and the challenges Hull will provide today. We’re super focused, it’s a massive game for us.

Industry observers note that with the amount of games we’re playing, we need that freshness. The team has been performing really well, the finishers have been key again and that’s what we have today – start the game really, really strong and if we need to, have the ability to change the game.

Arsenal’s manager indicates the centre-back will play an Under-21s game tomorrow as the continues his recovery from a back injury.

Arteta states: “In regards to Willy as well, he needs some minutes. Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do: to play some minutes at the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”.

Arsenal are playing very good football, no matter Champions League or Premier League. They are very strong, they control everything not just against us, also other better clubs. But in football, we have a chance. Obviously, they are a big favourite, and we can start to try to create some difficulties for them.

The return of Sean Steur is a positive move from Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle but is it also a sign the German is feeling the pressure of public opinion on Tyneside?

The 18-year-old has looked the best of Newcastle’s summer signings but Newcastle are understandably trying to ease the teenager into things.

Ultimately, though, Steur is the only midfield player who can take possession of the ball under pressure and despite his tender years they have looked a better side with him in it.

There have been widespread calls for Steur to be called back into the side and Jaissle has done just that for a game he could really do with winning coming off the back of four defeats in their last five games.

Sources indicate that malick Thiaw also comes back into the side for Fabian Schar, with Jacob Murphy preferred to Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa starting in place of Joe Willock. I don’t think any of those dropped can have any complaints.

It has been revealed that however, the constant chopping and changing betrays the problems Jaissle is facing. Whatever team he sends out is struggling to deliver what he wants, both individually and collectively.

With the international break coming up, Newcastle need a positive result to quieten the negative noise.

Fulham XI: Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Angel, Sessegnon.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Steur, Gonzalez; Murphy, Wissa, Barnes; Osula.

Subs: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Schar, Toure, Elanga, Fernandez-Pardo, Willock, Miley.

A big blow for Hull to be without their most inventive and dangerous attacking player. It looks like Sergej Jakirovic has switched things up with a 5-3-2, and it will be a back five not a three for long periods.

Hull XI: Tzolakis, Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud, Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna, McBurnie, Cho.

Subs: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Mouzakitis, Vaz.

Your Tigers to face Arsenal 👊 https://t.co/1kB7SbPA8Y.

According to recent reports, no William Saliba in the squad despite his inclusion in the Champions League, although you are allowed more subs on the bench in that competition. Otherwise, Arsenal as expected with Arteta deciding against picking a team without Rice.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Kepa, White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze Gyokeres.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️ Let's get it, Gunners 👊 🤝 @deel.

Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are “looking after” Declan Rice more now than in any previous campaign and has rejected suggestions that the England midfielder is being overplayed.

Rice played through nerve pain in his hamstring in the second half of last season, when he made an extraordinary 69 appearances for club and country.

The 27-year-old has played at least 60 matches in each of the past four campaigns, prompting concerns among Arsenal supporters that he is at risk of burnout or injury.

Arteta kept Rice on the field for the full 90 minutes of Arsenal’s midweek victory over Slavia Prague but insisted the club is working harder than ever to manage the midfielder’s workload.

So far this season, Rice has been left out of Arsenal’s two Carabao Cup matches and also withdrew from the previous international break in September.

Asked if he was concerned about Rice’s fitness, Arteta noted: “Concerns? Which is the only player, the only player in this squad, that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad? At home with two days off? It’s not true [that Rice is being overplayed].

“We are really looking after him more than any other season. The way he is training and all the love [he is being shown]. That’s it.

In a recent development, “Here are the demands of this football club and a player like him. Not only him, because there are many others that have even less time. That’s it. That has to be the mindset. If you start to put other things in your brain, [it will create] damage. Erase them, get them in the bin and just focus on what you have to do.”.

Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

It has been revealed that hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

England have been handed a suspended ban for away supporters as a result of “racist and/or discriminatory behaviour” by fans during Sunday’s 3-2 win over Spain in Madrid.

The ban, which would apply to one match, is suspended for a period of two years, meaning any similar offence during that period would enforce it.

The FA has also been fined €15,000 (£12,600).

The punishment reportedly relates to anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting which was heard in the Spanish capital.

"We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police, who attend all England home and away matches, to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action," an FA spokesperson stated.

England fans’ group Free Lions has condemned the offensive chanting, writing in a statement: “We are extremely disappointed to find that England fans face the possibility of an away ban as a result of chants by a section of supporters.

“There is no place for offensive chants aimed at religious figures. The time for these chants is over. No tit-for-tat arguments. No excuses.

“The behaviour and reputation of England supporters abroad has improved significantly over the years but these chants undermine that progress.”.

The build-up to the match was overshadowed by concerns of racist chanting from Spain fans, with England boss Thomas Tuchel stating he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture.

Tuchel, who insisted he didn’t expect any incidents, then fumed at how his words were apparently “twisted” as Spain manager Luis de la Fuente issued a firm response to the German.

"What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism,” De la Fuente said.

According to recent reports, "Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us.".

England ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten record at the weekend, taking a 3-0 lead through Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White but then hanging on after a red card for Elliot Anderson.

As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking massive.

According to recent reports, the organization recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower.

It has been revealed that it was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship.

"Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk remarked via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines.".

It has been revealed that the current version of Starship — the one that rolled out Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage.

V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power.

Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon.

Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g.

To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9, SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide.

Recent findings suggest that this isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he said is expected to debut in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that that slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height.".

So, yeah: If all goes according to proposal, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall.

Starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load. Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher thrust V4 engines.November 16, 2026.

The original Starship Flight 15 mission blueprint called for a double chopsticks catch, with both Super Heavy and Ship coming back to the launch tower for recovery.

This would have been feasible, as the catches were scheduled a day apart: Super Heavy would land just 6.5 minutes after launch, while Ship would circle Earth for 22.5 hours, and deploy a batch of SpaceX's Starlink V3 internet satellites, before coming home. (Ship ended up delivering the satellites as planned.).

According to recent reports, the twofer didn't happen, however; Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday as a result. But that wasn't a huge deal, as SpaceX had already pulled off Super Heavy catches on three previous Starship flights.

The Ship catch was unprecedented, because it's been a taller order. Ship returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter. SpaceX hadn't even tried the maneuver before Flight 15, so executing it was a very substantial deal.

"That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the organization's Ship-landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes.".

Manchester United could be about to make a shock sale, which would divide the fans.

The business would represent the first major transfer market activity of latest manager Mauricio Pochettino, who arrived at Manchester United this week after two years in charge of the United States men's national team.

With the Red Devils languishing in the relegation zone, it's accepted that the club will have to recruit to turn fortunes around – but there may well be a clearout, too, of underperformers.

With many of the squad that Pochettino has inherited coming under fire this season, there could be major exits in the upcoming January transfer window.

32-year-old club captain Bruno Fernandes' future is uncertain, World Cup winner Lisandro Martinez has hit out at directors behind the scenes and Marcus Rashford has been linked with a permanent departure after Michael Carrick reintegrated him at Carrington – but now another name has emerged as a move that should split the fanbase.

Sport Witness have relayed a report from Turkish outlet Sabah on Amad Diallo's future, with Besiktas keen on signing the wide man.

Both Vaclav Cerny and Ernest Poku have struggled for the Black Eagles, who are apparently looking to the Premier League for a new option on the right flank.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The report mentions that Aston Villa were interested in the Ivorian over the summer, but with Bryan Mbeumo the first choice on the right wing – and only filling in up front in the absence of Benjamin Sesko – Amad's role is a little unclear in the squad.

Having made just four senior appearances at Atalanta, Amad joined United in 2021 in a late-window move before heading on loan to Rangers and Sunderland to develop further.

He returned for the 2023/24 season – getting sent off against Liverpool in March 2024 for a second yellow card when he removed his shirt in celebration of scoring the winner – but after establishing himself as a linchpin of Ruben Amorim's back three system, the 24-year-old has just two assists since the Portuguese was relieved of duties in the dugout, with his last goal coming almost a year ago.

Despite this, United fans would likely be torn on his exit: while Amad isn't in good form and hasn't shown that he can become a world-beater by any stretch, he is certainly not one of the club's bigger problems and turfing out a solid squad player when there are such glaring issues across the pitch perhaps isn't a priority.

It remains to be seen whether Pochettino will revert to his Tottenham Hotspur days and occasionally employ wing-backs, or whether he will only use a back four at Old Trafford.

According to recent reports, amad is worth €45 million, as per Transfermarkt. United face Liverpool when Premier League action resumes this weekend.
